## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Chattupāhana-sikkhāpada* ("Rule on Sunshades and Sandals") is the eighty-fourth pācittiya rule of the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who uses both a sunshade (*chatta*) and sandals (*upāhanā*) incurs an offense that must be confessed [SuttaCentral]. In the word commentary (*padabhājanīya*), an exception is made for a nun who is ill (*gilānā*), defined as one who is not comfortable without a sunshade and sandals, whereas one who is healthy (*agilānā*) is comfortable without them [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary further specifies three types of sunshade—white cloth (*setacchatta*), rush matting (*kilañjacchatta*), and leaf (*paṇṇacchatta*)—constructed with circular bindings (*maṇḍalabaddha*) and ribs (*salākabaddha*), while *upāhanā* is left unglossed, as discussed also in the *Samantapāsādikā* in relation to Sekhiya 57 [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels for the rule are widespread across early Buddhist Vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Parallels exist in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra (Pācittiya 84), as well as in the Dharmaguptaka (*pācittiya* 158), Mahīśāsaka (*pācittiya* 142/157), Sarvāstivāda (*pācittiya* 148/149), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Tibetan and Chinese *pācittiya* 131), Mahāsaṅghika (*pācittiya* 112), and the Sanskrit Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga (*pācittiya* 112) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal formulaic reuse with 111 texts, most notably Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 85 (sharing §§0.1–2.1.5), Pāṭidesanīya 1 and 2–8, and other Vibhaṅga chapters, alongside cross-language alignments with the Tibetan Vinayavibhaṅga [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
